card.statement: Take $n=0$ and $m=1$, so that $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{so}_{3}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$. If the standard basis (= canonical basis) $\{u_{i}\mid i\in{\mathbb{Z}}\}$ for $\mathbb{V}$ is indexed by ${\mathbb{Z}}$, then $\mathbb{V}$ admits an $\imath$ canonical basis $\{u_{0},u_{-i},u_{i}+v^{-1}u_{-i}\mid i\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}\}$ and a dual $\imath$ canonical basis $\{u_{0},u_{-i},u_{i}-vu_{-i}\mid i\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}\}$.
card.label: Example 5.3

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
